question: A trader allows a discount of 10% on marked price. How much percent above the cost price should he mark his goods so as to make a profit of 17%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio formula: MP / CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%)

MP / CP = (100 + 17) / (100 − 10)

MP / CP = 117 / 90 = 1.3 / 1

Mark-up ratio = (1.3 − 1) / 1 = 0.3

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Discount = 10%, Profit = 17%

Formula Used: SP = CP × (1 + P/100); SP = MP × (1 − D/100)
